usual_baseline: Where a fast-track clinic exists, most are seen quickly: 70.8% by rheumatology within 24 hours [2889], all within 3 days [2933]. Outside a pathway it is poor: steroids 34%, rheumatology referral 55%, ultrasound 15% [2938]. Written information is patchy: 54% [2933], leaflets 43% of sites [2883]. Ophthalmology within 24 hours 50% with visual symptoms [2889].
fix_that_works: An SDEC pathway with a streamlined ultrasound order, teaching, posters and a probability score: ultrasound 15% to 77%, referral 55% to 77%, steroids 34% to 54% [2938]. Registrar hot clinics and more ultrasound capacity: referral to review 2.7 to 1.6 days, biopsy 41% to 7.5% [2898]. Regional feedback: pathways 2 to 6 sites, leaflets 43% to 80% [2883].
fix_that_fails: Time to rheumatology assessment did not change (1 to 1.5 days) [2938]. Steroid card provision did not change after regional feedback, and steroid taper protocols went from 8 to 7 sites [2883].
consultant_advice: Speed of review is usually good where a clinic exists, so don't re-audit it there. The gaps are steroids started before referral, written information and bone protection. Audit the front door, such as ED or SDEC, where the pathway is often not used.
